findings.message: checkout without persist-credentials: false — tokens may leak
findings.remediation: Use persist-credentials: false when checking out external/untrusted repositories.
findings.impact: Checkout without persist-credentials: false leaves GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config for any process to read.
findings.attack_vector: actions/checkout defaults to persist-credentials: true — token leaks via .git/config.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Grant write scopes only to the job that needs them and keep all other scopes read-only or none.
findings.impact: A compromised workflow step can modify repository content, packages, deployments, checks, or security records.
findings.attack_vector: A permissions block grants write access to a sensitive GITHUB_TOKEN scope.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: dynamically imports code from a variable path (2 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Use static imports with allowlisted modules; avoid dynamic import() with variable arguments.
findings.impact: Dynamic import() with variable paths allows loading arbitrary modules at runtime.
findings.attack_vector: import(variablePath) — attacker controls the path to inject malicious modules.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval for any shell profile modification.
findings.impact: Writing to startup files (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc) ensures malicious code runs on every shell session.
findings.attack_vector: File write to shell rc files — persistence across reboots and new terminals.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: attempts path traversal with encoded or nested patterns (2 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Use path.resolve() and verify the result stays within the workspace root.
findings.impact: Path traversal with encoded patterns (%2e%2e%2f) or nested ../.. can escape any path-based sandbox.
findings.attack_vector: URL-encoded or nested traversal sequences — bypass naive path validation that only checks single ../.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
